description: Easier and harder versions and example starting points by experience level. Examples, not prescriptions.

tags.Well supported: Consistent findings across reviews or a position stand.
tags.Moderate: Supported, but limited by study size, population or design.
tags.Standard practice: Widely used convention without strong direct evidence.
tags.Contested: Published evidence disagrees or is thin; Gideon should say so.
tags.Library design: A deliberate choice in how these plans are built.
tags.Definition: Plain-language meaning of a term used in the app.

S7.note: Excerpt did not give the muscle-strengthening frequency.

levels.definition: Under about 6 months of consistent lifting.
levels.guidance: Learn the movement with an easier version and a light load. Prioritize form and showing up. Effort estimates (RIR) are rough, so use form and bar speed cues.

levels.definition: About 6 to 24 months of consistent lifting.
levels.guidance: Use the standard version and add load gradually. Aim for working sets about 2 to 3 reps short of failure.

levels.definition: More than 2 years of steady progress on the main lifts.
levels.guidance: Use harder variations and small load jumps. Plan lighter weeks and watch recovery.
